transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ChatGPT. What brings you in today?

Ever since they cut my hours and dumped all this paperwork on me, I just haven’t been handling it well and I feel like I’m reacting all wrong to everything at work. It's just gotten to the point where I felt like I needed to talk to someone about it.
Have you been feeling this way only since the work changes, or have you also had similar worry, low mood, or stress in other parts of your life for at least 6 months?

No, I've never really dealt with anything like this before. It only started about a month ago, maybe a week or two after they cut my hours and put me on all that paperwork. Before this work stuff happened, I was doing just fine.
Since this started, have you had symptoms like feeling very down, losing interest in things, or feeling unusually anxious most days?

Yes, I'm constantly on edge and feel like I'm on the verge of snapping or tearing up over tiny mistakes at work. I've also stopped doing things I usually love, like my rec league and weekend side jobs with friends, because I'm just too wound up and embarrassed about how I'm handling everything. It really feels like this stress is spilling over into every part of my life.
Have these work-related feelings caused problems at home, with friends, or in your day-to-day functioning, and if so how much?

Yes, it's really messed up my life. My work slipped so much that I actually got a written warning, and I've stopped going to my rec league and doing side jobs with my buddies, which has hurt my income and social life. My sister actually had to urge me to get help because she saw how it was spilling over into everything.
Have your symptoms started to improve now that you’ve been away from the work stressor, or do they keep going even when the work situation is not on your mind?

Actually, I'm not away from the stressor at all—I'm still working there, so it's ongoing and constantly on my mind. But I really feel like if they would just put me back on regular crew work and things settled down, this stress and falling apart wouldn't drag on for more than a few months after that.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or feeling like life isn’t worth living since this started?

No, nothing like that, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself. I'm definitely feeling really stressed, overwhelmed, and embarrassed about how I'm handling things at work, but I've never wanted to end my life or anything.
If the work stress were to end or improve, do you think your symptoms would go away within about 6 months, or have they already been lasting that long without improvement?

This has only been going on for about a month now, so it hasn't been lasting that long. I really think that if they put me back on regular crew work or things settled down, this stress and struggling wouldn't drag on for more than a few months after that.
Have you ever had a period before this where you felt similarly overwhelmed, anxious, or unable to cope with stress, even if it was for a different reason?
No, I've never really felt this way before. This level of stress and struggling to cope is definitely a first for me.
Have you had any symptoms like hallucinations, manic episodes, or substance use that could better explain how overwhelmed and distressed you’ve been feeling?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that at all. I don't have hallucinations, manic episodes, or any issues with drinking or drugs. It's really just this work situation that has me so stressed out.
Has there been a specific event at work that felt especially upsetting or traumatic, or is it more the ongoing stress of the job changes and workload?

It’s really a mix of both. It started with specific things like suddenly cutting my hours, passing me over for a crew lead role I was promised, and dumping paperwork on me that I wasn't trained to do. But what's really wearing me down now is the daily, ongoing stress of trying to keep up with it and constantly getting criticized.
Did your symptoms start within a few days of the work change, or did they begin more gradually over the following weeks?

It didn't start the very next day, but it happened pretty fast. The feelings of being on edge and not handling things well really kicked in about a week or two after they cut my hours and switched me to the paperwork.
Do you feel your symptoms are mainly tied to this work situation, or have you also been feeling depressed or anxious in other areas of life even when you are away from work?

They definitely started because of the work situation, and I'm sure they'd go away if things there just went back to normal. But now, the stress has spilled over so much that I feel anxious and wound up even when I'm off the clock. It's got me avoiding my rec league and hanging out with my friends because I just can't shake it.

Did your symptoms begin within a few days of the work changes, or did they start more gradually over the following weeks? This helps me tell whether this is more like an acute stress reaction or an adjustment problem.

Like I mentioned, it wasn't the very next day, but it kicked in pretty quickly. The stress really started about a week or two after they cut my hours and switched me to the paperwork. It just took a little bit of time for the reality of trying to keep up with the new tasks to build up.
Have you had any period of feeling numb, detached, or like things around you weren't real since this started, or is it mainly ongoing stress, anxiety, and trouble coping with the work changes?

No, I haven't felt numb or detached, and everything feels all too real. It's definitely the latter—I'm just constantly stressed, wound up, and struggling to cope with the hours cut and all this paperwork.
